exposure: Cesarean section type (elective, emergency, non-emergency/medically necessary)
outcome: population attributable risk of pregestational obesity for caesarean section
cohort: 2309 pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy who gave birth at a public hospital in the Metropolitan Region of Santiago, Chile in 2015
finding: Pregestational obesity was found to increase the risk of both overall and elective caesarean delivery in this Chilean cohort.
mod_finding: This study found that pregestational obesity was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery, including both elective and emergency cesarean deliveries.
